events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.12 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride (Clarke Quay → Sentosa Beach Station), so distance variation flows into the fare: 10.9 km driven vs 7.9 km optimal, +3.0 km / +38% [F1], with total charged $26.46 made up of base $3.90, distance $15.33 and time $5.76 [F6]. One off-route segment is on the record: 18:32–18:39, 3.32 km where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km [F3]. Under RD-1 each off-route segment must be reviewed against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and any segment not excused is an unexcused detour [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not rescue the segment. No traffic incident is recorded near the route in the trip window [F12], and the only traffic facts are speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway [F10][F11]; band 3 is not band 1 or 2, and a speed band alone does not exempt a segment [RD-4]. So the driver's congestion excuse fails at RD-4(a)/(c) [F12][RD-4].

RD-5 is the decisive question on F3. I read the chat in context: at 18:28 the driver asked “Traffic ahead on Kampong Bahru Road is building up, ok if I go round via Outram Road?” [F7]. That is a question, not a consent [F7]. The chat record holds exactly one message and it is fully timestamped, so no rider reply exists, and none exists before the segment start (18:32) [F8][F3]. The driver's statement that “no objection, so I took it” was written after the trip, is not part of the chat, and is a claim of agreement rather than the rider's consent [F9][RD-5]. With the chat record complete and holding no rider agreement before 18:32, the correct finding is “counts”, not “undetermined” — nothing about the message's meaning or timing is unsettled [F7][F8][RD-5].

RD-3 does not apply: the rider named no place and no stop is measured in this segment; the ride's destination was Sentosa Beach Station and no pick-up/drop-off change was agreed [F3][RD-3].

The refund therefore covers only the extra kilometres of the unexcused segment, not the whole excess billed. The trace formula uses the metered distance rate: $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.4064/km, and the published rate is $1.41/km [F6]. Computing: 2.21 km × $1.4064/km = $3.11; 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The stronger figure is $3.12, consistent with the rider being billed $1.41 per extra km [F4]. The remainder of the +3.0 km extra (about 0.79 km, $1.09) is not attributable to the measured unexcused segment and is not refunded [F1][F3][F6][RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this case does not make the driver “repeated” and no account flag attaches [F15][RD-6]. F14 (rider profile) and F15 play no part in deciding the route question [F14][F15].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your Clarke Quay to Sentosa Beach Station trip. Your driver went one way off the route for about 7 minutes, adding roughly 2.2 km. He asked before taking that turn but you didn't agree, and the extra distance wasn't excused by traffic or anything else. We're refunding $3.12 for those extra kilometres. It comes to you as a Ryde voucher, not cash. The rest of the distance difference isn't covered, because it isn't tied to that off-route stretch. No action is being taken against the driver's account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the Clarke Quay to Sentosa Beach Station trip. One off-route stretch of about 3.3 km was recorded, where the normal route would have been about 1.1 km. You asked the rider about going round via Outram Road, but no agreement was given before you took it, and the traffic conditions on record don't exempt that stretch. We're refunding the rider $3.12 as a Ryde voucher for the extra 2.2 km. No action is being taken against your account.
